reports.title: Deere Reports Net Income of $1.051 Billion for Fourth Quarter, $4.860 Billion for Fiscal Year

guidance.heading: Company Outlook & Summary
section: Net income attributable to Deere & Company for fiscal 2027 is forecasted to be in a range of $4.50 to $5.25 billion. The forecast includes an estimated one-time, non-cash pension settlement charge of $0.25 to $0.40 billion associated with a voluntary lump-sum payment option for certain U.S. salaried retirees.

“As we enter fiscal 2027, we’re seeing early signs of improvement in large agriculture, led by North America,” said May. “Given continued uncertainty in key end markets, our outlook reflects a wider range of outcomes. Even so, we’re well positioned to capture the opportunities ahead by delivering solutions that improve our customers’ productivity and profitability, creating lasting value for our shareholders.”

desk.headline: Net sales of $10.51bn beat; EPS of $3.89 missed; FY27 net income outlook of $4.50–5.25bn below consensus
results: Net sales slipped 0.6% to $10.51bn, above the $10.34bn estimate; diluted EPS of $3.89 was below the $4.06 estimate.
Large farm equipment remained weak: Production & Precision Ag sales fell 15% on lower volumes and profit dropped 33%.
Small Ag & Turf (+10%) and Construction & Forestry (+12%) grew on volume and pricing, though construction profit dipped 3%.
Financial Services earned $231m, down 21% on tighter spreads, a smaller portfolio and higher credit provisions.
Full year: net income $4.86bn (-3%); operating cash flow $5.98bn; $796m spent on buybacks and $1.75bn on dividends.

guidance.summary: First FY27 outlook: net income of $4.50–5.25bn, including a one-off $0.25–0.40bn pension charge, below the $5.91bn analysts expected. Large-ag sales are seen up 5–15%.

points: CEO John May pointed to early signs of a large-ag recovery, led by North America.
He said continued uncertainty in key markets is why the FY27 range is unusually wide.
Slides show North American combine dealer stocks at 4% of retail sales, down from 8%, but large-tractor stocks up to 31% from 23%.
Deere kept its cash priorities: an A credit rating, then investment, a 25–35% mid-cycle dividend payout, and buybacks with remaining cash.
Deere booked $383m of tariff recoveries in FY26; Reuters reported construction sales are getting support from US data-centre building.
call.source: Earnings call slides (Exhibit 99.2) and CEO comments in the press release; Reuters via AOL, 25 Nov 2026. No full call transcript found.

watch: Whether North American large-ag orders firm up enough to support the 5–15% sales growth target.
Large-tractor dealer inventory, which rose to 31% of retail sales.
Size of the pension settlement charge and where FY27 profit lands in the wide range.
